Hi Priya / Sam — looping back with practical guidance. Summary up front: Redwood SDKs support configurable retry policies, automatic handling of 429s with Retry-After respect, idempotency keys for generation requests, and separate quota buckets for generation vs embeddings/rerankers. See attached samples and our internal rate-limit doc.

SDK setup (recommended):
- Python: pip install redwood-inference; use RedwoodClient(api_key=...) or configure short-lived tokens for server-side apps.
- Node: npm i @redwood/inference; same auth model.

Auth & token guidance:
- For server-to-server flows, use short-lived bearer tokens (rotate using your KMS) or API keys scoped to project. We support integration with AWS KMS and customer HSMs for Private deployments.
- Tokens should be passed in Authorization: Bearer <token>. For long-running jobs, mint new tokens periodically.

Routing & model variants:
- Route requests by region/model via client config; runtime will automatically fallback to compatible variants when capacity constrained (can be controlled via routingPolicy).
- For low-latency critical paths, pin to a dedicated model variant in Redwood Dedicated.

Structured output / tool-calling:
- Our function-calling uses a JSON-schema style declaration; responses include a canonical tool_call field for deterministic parsing. SDK includes helpers to validate and deserialize.

Embeddings & reranker notes:
- Embedding endpoints have separate quotas and rate limits from generation. We recommend batching embeddings (batch size 256–1024 depending on vector dimension) and using the async batch endpoint for very large jobs.
- Reranker calls are lightweight but have their own concurrency limits; we can allocate higher quota for rerankers on Dedicated plans.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-samples.zip (examples), api-rate-limits.md (summary doc)

Subject: RE: ACME integration — rate limits & retry strategy (technical details)

Hi Priya / Sam — quick technical recommendations on rate limiting, retries and idempotency based on your ~150 QPS peak and embedding batch profile.

1) Quotas & rate-limit model (server-side):
- Per-tenant token/sec and requests/sec limits. Generation and embeddings/reranker have separate quota buckets by default.
- We support burst tokens for short spikes; sustained traffic above quota will receive 429 responses with Retry-After headers.

2) 429 handling & Retry-After:
- Always respect Retry-After when provided. If Retry-After is absent, fall back to client-side backoff policy (see below).
- Our service returns X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, and X-RateLimit-Reset (unix epoch seconds) on non-error responses for monitoring.

3) Idempotency & request IDs:
- For deterministic generation requests (where duplicate processing is harmful), include an Idempotency-Key header on the client: Idempotency-Key: <uuid-v4>. Redwood will dedupe identical keys for a 24h window for the same customer/model/route.
- Also send a Client-Request-Id (opaque) per request; this is logged and surfaced in debug traces.

4) Recommended client retry/backoff (example):
- Retry on 429 and 5xx (500/502/503/504), but do NOT retry on 400/401/403/422.
- Exponential backoff with jitter:
  initial = 500ms, max = 10s, factor = 2.0, max_retries = 5
  e.g. sleep = min(max, initial * factor^attempt) * (0.5 + random())
- For streaming/long-poll requests, consider client-side streaming resumption instead of blind retries.

5) Idempotency edge cases & partial responses:
- If a request produced partial output before a server error, having an Idempotency-Key allows the client to safely re-issue and either receive the original result or a deterministic duplicate.
- For streaming responses where partial tokens were delivered, we recommend checkpointing by request-id and sequence numbers.

6) SDK defaults & instrumentation:
- Our SDKs expose a RetryPolicy object (backoff settings, retryable status codes, max attempts) and automatically inject Client-Request-Id if absent.
- SDK emits metrics and traces for: request latency, backend_429_count, retry_count, and idempotency_conflicts.

7) Practical tuning for ACME profile:
- For 150 QPS peak with avg ~800 tokens/request, start with per-client concurrent request limit of 50 and use batching for embeddings jobs (batch size ~512), offload large embedding batches to async batch endpoint during off-peak windows.
- Set client max_retries=4, initial_backoff=400ms, max_backoff=8s as a conservative starting point. Adjust based on observed Retry-After patterns.

I've attached a short PDF with the rate-limit guidelines and a sample pseudocode snippet you can drop into your HTTP client. Happy to walk through this in the sync — I can cover retry tuning and idempotency behavior end-to-end.

Cheers,
